summary: The original is a nearly-black strip that fires a single dim blue-white spark outward from centre roughly every 2.5 s, each fading to nothing in ~0.7 s; the port fires the same centre-launched outward pair but never fades them, so the whole strip rails to 255,255,255 within ~1 s and its steady state is a random ~50/50 pure-white/pure-black barcode.
observations: Neither side exposes any controls (probe: 'no settable controls' on both) — control surfaces match; both compile and run with no compile/runtime error.

ORIGINAL, opening regime (t=0..0.5 s, --label regime-open/dump-ev, 60 px @20 fps): a symmetric fountain burst from the centre. --dump shows lit pixels 26-32 at t=0.00 (px27,31,32 at 255,255,255; px26/28 bluish 45,59,108 / 49,63,112), spreading to 15..42 at t=0.20 and 11..46 at t=0.30. The lit COUNT stays ~12-13 while the span grows to 37 px — i.e. a thin moving shell with a short fading tail, not a filled block.

ORIGINAL, steady regime (everything after ~0.5 s): mean brightness is 0 for 96% of frames. Over 120 s @20 fps only 33 frames-groups register meanBrightness>0, all with max 1. --skip 60 waterfall shows ~13 individual spark arcs in 30 s => launch rate ~0.4 sparks/s (one every ~2.3 s).

ORIGINAL single-spark trajectory (--label spark-trace, dense dump at t=62.90..63.70): px32 at 27,40,83 -> px42 at 6,14,42 (+0.2 s) -> px48 at 1,5,18 (+0.4 s) -> px51 at 0,0,1 (+0.6 s) -> black by +0.8 s. So each spark DECELERATES (10, 6, 3 px per 0.2 s), travels ~20 px, and fades roughly exponentially over ~0.7 s. Colour is strongly blue-dominant (B ~2-3x R) and never re-brightens.

PORT, opening: launches in the right place with the right colour family — t=0.00 has px28 and px31 at 255,255,255 with px29/30 at 10,17,83 and 16,24,95 (same blue-white family as the original). The outward front expands symmetrically at ~43 px/s (orig ~57 px/s).

PORT, core defect: the trail NEVER decays. --dump at 20 fps: t=0.10 px24-35 all 255,255,255; t=0.20 px21-38; t=0.30 px18-42 (lit count 24 over a 26 px span = solid). By t=2 s all 60 px are 255,255,255 and stay there. meanBrightness series: 10,27,42,...,225,233,...,251 and pinned at 251 from ~1.6 s to ~35 s.

PORT steady state is BINARY, not decayed. Value histogram of whole frames at t=60/90/120/150/179 s: only two values ever present — {0,0,0} and {255,255,255} (36/24, 32/28, 29/31, 30/30, 30/30). The --skip 60 waterfall is a flickering white/black barcode with no colour, no arcs and no centre symmetry. Original over the same window: essentially black with occasional dim blue arcs (statsSummary meanBrightness avg 0.1 vs port 146.4).

Saturation is not an artefact of the harness default rig or rate. fps sweep 2/3/5/10/20/40/80 (20 s each): port mean 146/180/209/233/245/242/191 — railed at every rate. Pixel sweep 12/30/60/150/300/600 px: port mean 171/240/230/234/223/201 — railed at every size. Seeds 7 and 1234 over 30 s: port mean 247 both. Original stays mean 0-8 throughout.

Neither side is frame-rate coupled in its front speed: at t=0.30 s the orig front sits at px47 (10 fps) vs px45 (40 fps), the port at px43 (10 fps) vs px41 (40 fps). Both are time-based; the divergence is decay/persistence, not dt handling.

brightnessTrend at baseline: orig 'volatile' (spark bursts on black), port 'rising' (10 -> 251). zeroMotionFrames 109/120 orig vs 85/120 port; motionLit avg 4.8 orig vs 5.1 port — the motion stats alone hide the failure, the pixel dumps do not.
feedback: The single decisive bug: the port's spark/trail buffer is never faded. Every pixel a spark passes over stays at full 255,255,255 forever, so the strip fills to solid white in about 1 s and never recovers. Whatever per-frame decay the original applies to its trail is either missing, or is being applied as a max/accumulate instead of a multiply-down.

Target behaviour to reproduce, measured on the original at 60 px / 20 fps: a spark launched from the centre should be at max ~83 (blue-white, e.g. 27,40,83) at birth and decay to black in ~0.7 s, following roughly 83 -> 42 -> 18 -> 1 -> 0 sampled every 0.2 s. The port's launch colour (10,17,83 at px29) is correct; its brightness envelope is not.

The port also over-drives spark brightness: original steady-state sparks peak around 80-110 in the blue channel and only the t=0 opening burst reaches 255. The port writes 255,255,255 for essentially every touched pixel, which flattens the blue-dominant palette to white. Preserve the B>G>R ratio at all brightnesses instead of clipping to white.

Spark lifetime/travel: the original's spark DECELERATES — 10 px in the first 0.2 s, then 6, then 3, dying after ~20 px of travel. The port's front advances at a near-constant ~43 px/s and never stops, sweeping the entire strip. Add the drag/deceleration term and let the spark die when its brightness reaches zero.

Launch rate: the original emits roughly 0.4 sparks/s (one every ~2.3 s), one or two at a time, from a point just right of the exact centre (px32 of 60), occasionally mirrored to the left. Confirm the port's spawn rate once the fade is fixed — under saturation it is unmeasurable, but the port's opening frames put two simultaneous sparks at px28 and px31 versus the original's wider 26-32 opening burst.

The original opens with a one-off multi-spark fountain burst (whole strip active for ~0.5 s, mean brightness 15->21->0) and then settles into the sparse single-spark regime. Keep that opening transient; it is real original behaviour, not warm-up noise.

After fixing the fade, re-check the steady state specifically with --skip 60 --seconds 30 --fps 20: the target is meanBrightness avg ~0.1 with isolated arcs, not a white field. Any port steady state above single-digit mean brightness on a 60 px strip is still wrong.
